source.build: Mythic Tactics.app (iOS, com.hexpion.hex05 1.6.0 build 566, installed on macOS)
source.note: Ids, names, rules text, keywords, realms, descend quests and the art of every card added in 1.6.0 come out of the shipped client. The 1.6.0 source is the iOS app rather than an Android package, so buildSha256 hashes its Data folder: `find . -type f | LC_ALL=C sort | tr '\n' '\0' | xargs -0 shasum -a 256 | shasum -a 256`, run inside MythicTactics.app/Data. Art of the cards that were already here was kept from the 1.5.7 Android build (c4749f723792ea37aa8ac5251f4096e282baaaa8fcd43cde192115cd7b38489f): the 1.6.0 art is the same pictures and differs only by texture compression, except icon_pass_xp, which the game redrew and was taken from 1.6.0. tier, cost, attack and health are not present in any build — they were carried in from an earlier dataset, and cost plus the god realms were checked against the running game on 1.5.7. Gods carry no Tier in any source; they are set to 6, the top Sanctum Tier, by hand. realmLock is hand-maintained the same way: the client says nothing about it, and the eight gods marked true were read off the game's Patron God screen on 1.5.7 (Ra, Tiamat, Zeus, Poseidon, Odin, Erlang Shen, Izanami, Samsin). It cannot be derived from the card text — Set names Niles twice and does not lock it. The two gods added in 1.6.0, Amaterasu and Tsukuyomi, are Kami per the 1.6.0 patch notes; their stats (20/10 and 18/12) and realmLock (false for both) were read off the running game on 1.6.0, as was Tier 6 for Eye of Heaven (s_04014). Balance changes in 1.6.0 that live only in runtime numbers — the {0}/{1} Medicine values — are not captured anywhere.

conventions.textPlaceholders: Rules text keeps {0}-style placeholders on purpose. Those numbers are not fixed — cards in play change what a Medicine is worth, so the game computes the value at runtime. Render the placeholder, do not try to fill it in.
conventions.medicineCost: Medicine spells have no cost. They are not bought with gold; Alchemy grants them, so a null cost on a medicine card is the right answer rather than a missing one.
conventions.godCost: Gods have no cost — a patron is chosen, not bought.
